exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly describes data transmitted in plaintext over unencrypted protocols, matching the core concern of plaintext transmission.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext transmission enables network sniffing attacks where adversaries can capture unencrypted data in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly describes downgrade attacks that force systems to use weaker protocol versions, exactly matching a TLS downgrade attack.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: TLS downgrade attacks aim to weaken encryption by forcing negotiation of older, less secure TLS versions or cipher suites.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Symmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Cipher suite negotiation governs which symmetric cryptographic algorithms are used, making this directly relevant to weak cipher selection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing certificate validation can be exploited by installing rogue root certificates to perform man-in-the-middle attacks without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can develop forged digital certificates to exploit systems that lack proper certificate validation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS allows adversaries to obtain and use certificates without needing to authenticate mutually, enabling impersonation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, stolen or forged certificates can be used to impersonate clients or servers in the communication channel.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transmitted Data Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks involve capturing and retransmitting previously valid PII requests, which constitutes manipulation of transmitted data.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Duplication
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks on PII requests involve duplicating captured network traffic and replaying it to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Encrypted Channel
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of HSTS allows connections to be downgraded from encrypted HTTPS to plaintext HTTP, undermining encrypted channel requirements.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Automated Exfiltration
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, adversaries can automate high-volume PII exfiltration without triggering throttling controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data Transfer Size Limits
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of rate limiting means there are no data transfer size constraints, enabling large-scale PII extraction.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: BGP route hijacking redirects network traffic through adversary-controlled infrastructure, enabling adversary-in-the-middle interception.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: BGP hijacking can bridge network boundaries by rerouting traffic across network perimeters through malicious route announcements.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS spoofing involves compromising or manipulating DNS servers to redirect traffic flow to adversary-controlled destinations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries gather DNS information to perform targeted DNS spoofing attacks that redirect legitimate traffic flows.
